title: Measuring the Mechanical Properties of Living Cells Using Atomic Force Microscopy
protocol: Calibrate the spring constant of the cantilever according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Clean the cantilever holder with ethanol before loading the cantilever into the AFM.
Load the cantilever into the AFM.
Install a clean glass slide onto the sample stage.
Adjust the laser beam and alignment according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Engage the AFM tip on the glass slide.
Realign the mirror to a photodiode reading of -2 V with the piezo withdrawn.
Perform a force spectroscopy measurement with a trigger point (maximum photodiode response) of +2 V.
Zoom in to the firm-contact region of the force curve after data acquisition is complete.
Perform a linear fit to this region to find the slope, which will be in V/nm.
Calculate the optical sensitivity using the reciprocal value of the slope.
Reset the mirror alignment to a free deflection of 0 V.
Calibrate the cantilever spring constant using a thermal-tune method.
Raise the scanner away from the sample stage after calibrating the InvOLS.
Begin capturing thermal data of the cantilever beam vibration.
Analyze the power spectrum of the thermal vibration with AFM software.
Perform a fit to the data segment centered at the fundamental resonance peak.
Install the Dish Heater accessory on the AFM stage if not already equipped.
Set the temperature to 37 °C and wait for 20 min for system stabilization.
Place the culture dish on the AFM stage and secure it using the clamp.
Apply a small drop of 37 °C culture medium to the tip of the AFM cantilever.
Lower the AFM head until the tip is just submerged in liquid.
Realign the laser beam on the cantilever using the top-view CCD camera.
Engage the AFM tip on a clean area of the culture dish.
Calibrate the InvOLS for the cantilever sensitivity in the liquid environment.
Perform calibration of the InvOLS against the bottom surface of a culture dish filled with cell culture media if cells are cultured on hydrogels.
Recalibrate the InvOLS whenever there is a change in laser beam alignment.
Take the InvOLS as the average value from several calibration curves for consistency.
Select a cell for indentation using an optical microscope.
Move the stage to position the cantilever above the selected cell so that the tip is located in the peri-nuclear region.
Withdraw the AFM cantilever from the sample surface while moving the sample stage to select a target cell.
Switch to Force Spectroscopy mode.
Set the Indentation rate within the range of 1-10 μm/sec.
Set the deflection trigger point to limit the maximum indenting force to avoid damage to cells.
Select the Relative triggering option to correct for any drift in the deflection signal.
Use a maximum force of 2 nN as a starting point, adjusting according to sample stiffness.
Set the force distance at least 5 μm to ensure the tip is fully detached from the cell between measurements.
Command the AFM to take a single force curve.
Collect at least three force curves at different locations in the peri-nuclei region of each cell.
Withdraw the tip after data collection is complete.
Repeat steps 3.1-3.6 for additional cells to gather sufficient statistical data on cell stiffness under a certain sample condition.
Measure typically 30 cells per condition.
Apply force-map mode to characterize stiffness distribution within a single cell.
Set a scan size to encompass the region of interest.
Set an appropriate resolution for the scan area.
Set indentation parameters as those selected for single force curves.
The AFM raster scans across the defined sample area and takes single force curves at each pixel in the specified region.
Analyze recorded force curves using a custom MATLAB procedure to calculate cell stiffness.
Identify contact point coordinates z0 and d0 for each data point in the force curve.
Perform a linear fit of the data points to the left of the point of interest.
Fit data points to the right with a Hertz model, starting from the selected initial point of contact up to the set maximum indentation (recommended 200-300 nm).
Calculate the relative RMS error for both fits at each point.
Select as the initial point of contact the one that attains the minimum total fitting error.
